objectives.name: Add the home television CRT practice console

objective.text: Add an interactable television connected to an old-console-style game system in Motel Room, Apartment and Home, including in-run and meta-home contexts. Interaction opens a dedicated original console-inspired CRT environment titled Beat the House, with selectable entries containing each of the eleven actual playable Games registry names and existing icons. Selecting any game uses its existing production practice/generation path, seed controls, rules and setup. Leave returns to the same CRT selector with useful selection and seed state retained; exiting the CRT returns to the originating room or title screen. The title-screen Games button opens this same environment. Preserve all supported generation seed options/defaults and practice setup, including Scratch Ticket machine stock of 100 of each ticket. Protect live run and meta money, Heat, time, inventory, progression, unlocks, RNG, save state and Continue. Deliver focused durable routing/state-boundary regression coverage, fresh native/Web input and visual acceptance, tested scoped main integration and exact existing NEXT deployment verification for 0.6.1.
objective.source: Erik Petersen's explicit 2026-11-19 feature request, room message Sentinel_9b2c20b4acbc8191981dcf794fa88be2, delegated by coordinator thread 6afc9600-f7f0-8191-926d-d8ae551e500c, followed by explicit visual correction Sentinel_83b6184147f88191a431dcfb7e571ccb at 06:45:18 UTC. The request authorizes a new agent and tested main-to-existing-NEXT delivery. Verified starting main and NEXT were 89403f389a5807e050a450cd27b1bd93b3a4a41e; isolated source checkout preserves unrelated dirty and unique work. The previous picker-like presentation is withdrawn before publication.
objective.visual_correction: Replace the withdrawn picker-like presentation with an actual curved 4:3 CRT matching the Beat the House palette, scanlines, bowed image and irregular analog text shake. Use a bespoke original SNES-era game-select hierarchy inspired by the era of Mario Kart, Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter without importing their artwork or logos. Preserve all eleven production practice games, generation options/defaults, room/title routes and isolation. Reduce Motion disables jitter. Requalify native/Web desktop and mobile edge hits, focus and navigation on the new presentation.

acceptance.description: Show all eleven actual playable games with canonical current names/icons in a bespoke original SNES-era game-select hierarchy inside a curved 4:3 CRT matching the Beat the House palette, with scanlines, bowed image and irregular analog text shake; Reduce Motion disables jitter. Withdraw the prior picker-like presentation before publication and requalify edge hits, focus and native/Web desktop/mobile navigation.
Verify title Games, Motel Room, Apartment, Home and meta-home entry, every game launch and Leave, selector state retention, cancel/back, CRT exit to the origin and repeated loops.
Retain every existing per-game seed/generation option and default through the production practice path; verify seed repeatability, game prerequisites and Scratch Ticket stock of 100 of each ticket.

Prove practice cannot leak money, Heat, time, inventory, progression, unlocks, RNG or save state into the real run or meta session, and cannot overwrite Continue. Qualify an ordinary autosave queued immediately before entry, an accepted save in flight, background/reload while in practice, real wager/Leave/CRT Exit and cold Continue/profile/meta retention; retain durable focused boundary regressions.

After exclusive runtime-window assignment, verify rendered native/Web layouts and keyboard/controller/mouse/touch navigation using fresh disposable QA state and approved E: guarded workloads, with material limits recorded.

After coordinator integration-window assignment, land only this tested feature through the existing reviewed main-to-NEXT workflow and verify exact remote/served commit, assets and feature smoke; record identity and test evidence without a stable release, tag or code-freeze claim.
